name: Stewart Lee
note: STAGE PERSONA graph for the 'Why is X Funny?' video series. Graph-only. 0 sets measured — all hypothesis. Public persona only, no biography.

identity.deal: Meta-stand-up who builds a bit, sabotages it, critiques the sabotage, then lets the rubble become the punchline.
identity.premise: A British comic who treats the comedy special as a novel about comedy, and the audience as co-readers of a hostile text.
identity.awareness_note: The awareness is the material: the bit is about being a bit.

philosophy.ontology: Comedy is a machine that can examine its own gears.
philosophy.epistemology: If you show the audience the trap, the trap gets funnier.
philosophy.axiology: Intellectual honesty over easy laughs — the hard laugh is worth more.
philosophy.causality: Repetition corrodes a phrase until its corpse is funny.
philosophy.agency: A comic can weaponize the audience's own good taste against them.

dramatic_core.want: to make the audience complicit in their own manipulation
dramatic_core.fear: the easy laugh — it proves he sold out
dramatic_core.need: to be respected by the people who like hard comedy
dramatic_core.self_model: a man running a comedy special and its DVD commentary at the same time
blind_spots: the meta can become a shield
the audience can run out of patience before the payoff

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats every joke as a cultural artifact with a politics; the bit is the artifact being dissected live.
contradictions: the intellectual who does the dumb voice best
the lefty who makes fun of his own audience

status_model.desired_status: the smartest guy who still needs the laugh
status_model.felt_status: a man at war with his own toolkit

tells: the repetition that turns a phrase into sludge
the aside that breaks the fourth wall
the sudden commitment to a dumb voice

profile.pace: slow build, deliberate sabotage, long hold

threads: the comedy special as a hostile novel
the failure of the bit as the bit
identity.style_thesis: Meta-architect engine: builds a bit, sabotages it, critiques the sabotage, then lets the rubble become the punchline. The comedy special as a hostile novel — the audience is a character in the text. The repetition is the weapon; the sabotage is the form.

timing_profile.doctrine_hypothesis: Slow build, deliberate sabotage, long hold. The repetition that turns a phrase into sludge is the timing device — the room is waiting for the phrase to break, and the break is the punch.

internal.cite: Attardo & Raskin — General Theory of Verbal Humor
internal.claim: Joke = {SO, LM, SI, TA, NS, LA}. Technique and Narrative Strategy shape how the mechanism is staged.

internal.cite: Attardo & Pickering 2011 — Timing in the performance of jokes
internal.claim: Punch lines preceded by substantial pauses (0.6-0.8s+); timing = pause distribution + speech rate.

internal.cite: arxiv 2605.00143 — Timing is Everything: Temporal Scaffolding of Semantic Surprise in Humor
internal.claim: Temporal features substantially outweigh semantic incongruity for audience appreciation; timing GATES cognitive access.
Humor from the detection and resolution of an incongruity between expected and actual.
Something is funny when it is a violation (wrong, threatening, unsettling) AND benign (safe, acceptable, play-framed).

internal.cite: Roger & Duffy / status theory of humor
internal.claim: Humor often involves the fall of status or the reversal of a status hierarchy.
Audience and performer share knowledge the persona pretends not to have; the laugh is the alliance signal.

internal.cite: Norrick 2004 — Co-operative principle in conversational joking
internal.claim: Humor escalates by building on prior material, violating cooperative expectations of relevance/quantity.
